skill.name: verify-release
skill.description: Compare release telemetry and recommend Go, Rollback, or Wait using LogBrew or supplied counts.
skill.summary: Assess deployment health against a previous release using comparable evidence.
skill.author: logbrewco

security_audit.summary: The static matches are Markdown formatting, a documented service endpoint, or release decision criteria rather than the alleged threats. The skill also directs deployment record creation and pipeline changes without explicit confirmation, which can affect production evidence.

remediation.issue: Deployment records and pipeline changes are requested without explicit confirmation.
remediation.suggestion: Verify deployment status and timestamps, then obtain user approval before creating records or changing the pipeline.

semantic_findings.title: Deployment records may be changed without confirmation
semantic_findings.description: The skill instructs the agent to record missing deployments as succeeded and add a command to the pipeline without requiring user confirmation. Incorrect records or pipeline changes can distort release comparisons.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instructions explicitly request a state-changing deployment record and pipeline modification, but do not require confirmation or verification of successful status.

content.value_statement: Release decisions can be difficult when error counts and traffic change together. Compare release evidence and receive a Go, Rollback, or Wait recommendation.
actual_capabilities: Compare a release with the previous release using LogBrew CLI or MCP data.
Examine trace error rates, traffic counts, and comparison limitations.
Identify unresolved issues first seen in the new release.
Compare error logs relative to traffic over equal-length windows.
Recommend Go, Rollback, or Wait with supporting evidence.
Assess user-supplied counts when no LogBrew tool is connected.
limitations: A release comparison provides evidence, not proof that code caused a change.
Missing comparisons, unavailable evidence, or insufficient traffic can require a Wait decision.
Recording deployments requires CLI account access; the MCP server is read-only.
A rollback involving a database migration requires a person to decide.

use_cases.title: Assess a production rollout
use_cases.description: Compare error rates and new issues before continuing a rollout.

use_cases.title: Investigate a canary
use_cases.description: Review traffic and failure evidence to decide whether to wait or roll back.

use_cases.title: Review exported counts
use_cases.description: Compare supplied request and error counts when LogBrew tools are unavailable.

prompt_templates.title: Basic release check
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether release [release] is safe to continue.

prompt_templates.title: Compare releases
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [new release] with [previous release] for [service] in [environment]. Report the evidence and decision.

prompt_templates.title: Use exported counts
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these equal-length windows: [new counts] and [previous counts]. Include traffic, errors, new error types, and deploy times.

prompt_templates.title: Review a rollout
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess [release] against [previous release] using [team traffic threshold]. Report new issues, normalized error logs, trace rates, limitations, and next checks.

output_examples.input: Assess a release with sufficient traffic and stable error rates.
output_examples.output: Decision: Go. Both releases have sufficient traffic, and the observed error rates are unchanged. No new issue affects a main user flow.

output_examples.input: Assess a release with too few traces for comparison.
output_examples.output: Decision: Wait. The new release has too little traffic for a reliable comparison. Recheck trace counts and error rates after more requests.

best_practices: Compare the same service and environment across equal-length windows.
Normalize error counts by traffic and apply your team traffic threshold.
Review limitations and verify deployment details before recording them.
anti_patterns: Do not treat missing telemetry as zero errors.
Do not assume a release caused an error solely because it preceded the error.
Do not create deployment records or modify pipelines without confirming the details and authorization.

faq.question: What decisions can the skill recommend?
faq.answer: It recommends Go, Rollback, or Wait based on available release evidence.

faq.question: Can I use it without LogBrew?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide request counts, error counts, new error types, and deploy times for equal-length windows.

faq.question: Does the skill prove a release caused an error?
faq.answer: No. The comparison provides evidence, but deployment order does not prove causality.

faq.question: How much traffic is enough?
faq.answer: The default is at least 100 traces per release in the compared window. A team threshold can replace it.

faq.question: Can the MCP server record deployments?
faq.answer: No. The skill describes the MCP server as read-only; recording requires CLI account access.

faq.question: Does the skill perform a rollback?
faq.answer: The documented workflow recommends a decision. It does not provide a command to perform a rollback.
